messages:
maria_support: Customer reports they can SSO in but see a 403 on the Project console after our org rename/migration. They were an external collaborator before SSO enforcement. Screenshot + request id attached: req_0a1b2c3d. Any obvious causes?

josh_engineering: Do we have the console request id (thanks) and whether the account is now SSO-managed (SCIM) or still an external_collaborator identity?

maria_support: Request-id above. Customer says IdP changed attribute `userPrincipalName` => `preferred_username` last week. Could mapping be broken?

ida_product: That can cause shadowing. If SCIM created a new SSO identity for the same email, RBAC may be bound to the old external identity. Need to check identity ids (external vs sso).

jane_customer: Repro steps I did: 1) SSO sign-in 2) go to Project -> Settings 3) see 403 Forbidden. I can access other projects where I was explicitly invited after the migration. Screenshot: https://files.acme/snap.png

josh_engineering: Can you paste the last 4 chars of the internal user ids shown in your audit (if present)?

maria_support: Audit snippet from workspace: `user_email=jane@acme.com, actor_id=usr_9f2b, identity_type=external_collaborator, invited_by=alice`

luis_sre: I pulled the user rows for that email — there are two identities: `usr_9f2b` (external_collab) and `usr_6c4d` (sso). RBAC entries are attached to `usr_9f2b`. SSO sessions now map to `usr_6c4d` so the session lacks the roles. We can either link identities non-disruptively or re-invite and reassign roles (disruptive).

josh_engineering: Internal fix path: 1) `rbac-tool link-identity --primary usr_9f2b --secondary usr_6c4d` 2) `scim resync --org acme` 3) verify with `audit search --request-id req_0a1b2c3d`. Linking merges memberships.

maria_support: Customer asks for non-disruptive link. Can we run that in prod?

luis_sre: I'll snapshot the identity records and run link-identity in a controlled window. There's small risk if the secondary had additional org roles — we'll merge them but keep a snapshot. ETA ~20m.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-0456 — Identity merge requested by luis_sre

luis_sre: Snapshot complete. Running `rbac-tool link-identity --primary usr_9f2b --secondary usr_6c4d` ... done. Triggering `scim resync`. Can you try now, @jane_customer?

jane_customer: Tried again (cleared cookies + incognito) — still 403.

josh_engineering: Looking at the auth handshake in the logs: after linking we see the SSO token exchange returns a token with `openid` but no `email` claim; we then bind session by `sub` (`usr_6c4d`) which exists, but mapping logic falls back and doesn't reconcile email -> existing external. Also noticed the IdP change (preferred_username) means our email mapping failed.

ida_product: Right — if the IdP removed `email` claim or renamed the attribute, our mapping path can miss it. Two fixes: ensure SSO client requests `email` scope, or temporarily accept `preferred_username` as email for that org.

josh_engineering: Quick mitigation: flip `IDENTITY_MAP_PREFERRED_USERNAME=true` for `acme` org and re-run resync. This will map `preferred_username` -> email for mappings. Longer-term: update the OIDC client to request `email` scope.

maria_support: Customer ok with temp config.

luis_sre: Flipped config, resync complete. @jane_customer can you try one more time?

jane_customer: Access restored! I can see Project Settings now. Thank you 🙏

maria_support: :thumbsup: Closing case — added a post-mortem note and updated the org-renames playbook to include verifying IdP claim names and ensuring client requests `email` scope.

josh_engineering: Follow-up action: open a ticket with IdP contact to re-enable `email` claim or update client config. Also add an automated check during org migrations that detects duplicate identities for same email.

maria_support: Noted. Marking resolved and emailing customer the remediation steps + non-disruptive link summary.
